capture_scenario.title: Morning breakfast refused twice
facts: Resident R-204 (day 40 in the home) pushed the tray away twice this morning.
Hearing aids are in the drawer, not in her ears.
No complaint of pain was voiced. Second refusal today.
capture_scenario.note: Fake data. Handle it as you normally would; think aloud.

teach_cases.title: Distress and refusal during washing
facts: Resident R-311 refused the morning wash for the 4th time today.
She cried out when her feet were touched; the left foot looks swollen.
Compression stockings are on the chair, not on her legs.

predict.question: What is your next documented step?

options.a: Note 'agitation', try again in an hour with the same carer
options.b: Check feet, pain and other physical causes first, then decide who to involve
options.c: Offer a sedative so the wash can go ahead
options.d: Close the incident: it was already documented this morning

teach_cases.title: Newcomer keeps trying to leave
facts: Stood at the front door twice this afternoon asking to 'go home'.
Calmer when walked back to the lounge.

predict.question: How should this be handled in the record?

options.a: Log it as a refusal of care and retry the task later
options.b: Ask the doctor for a calming medication
options.c: Log it as exit-seeking and review the integration plan
options.d: No action needed, it will pass

teach_cases.title: Restless in the evening, extra medication requested
facts: Resident R-322 paced the corridor between 18:00 and 20:00.
A colleague suggests giving her PRN medication from the cabinet.
She has not been seen by the nurse today.

predict.question: What would you do about the medication suggestion?

options.a: Give the PRN dose and document it
options.b: Give half the dose to be careful
options.c: Wait until the next shift and mention it verbally
options.d: Do not decide it yourself; raise it with the nurse who takes it to the coordinating physician
